disclaimer: A learning map, not an official exclusive taxonomy or an availability promise. Relationships and journeys illustrate possible uses, not mandatory dependencies. Billing labels and estimates come from the separate pricing catalog; a missing rate does not mean free. Cloud, region, edition, release state, and account requirements vary.

domains.name: Ingestion
domains.summary: Move database changes, application records, files, and events into the lakehouse.
domains.billingContext: Connector execution, data volume, storage, and networking can contribute to the bill.

domains.name: Data engineering
domains.summary: Transform and orchestrate repeatable batch and streaming workloads.
domains.billingContext: Estimate the compute used by each task or pipeline; orchestration is not a second copy of that compute.

domains.name: Analytics & BI
domains.summary: Query governed data and deliver dashboards, conversational analysis, and business insights.
domains.billingContext: Warehouse execution drives many BI costs; map the interface to its underlying compute and usage.

domains.name: AI & machine learning
domains.summary: Develop models and agents, retrieve context, run inference, and evaluate quality.
domains.billingContext: Training, serving capacity, tokens, retrieval, and evaluation may be separate cost drivers.

domains.name: Apps & databases
domains.summary: Deliver data applications and transactional Postgres services alongside the lakehouse.
domains.billingContext: An app can consume database, warehouse, or AI services in addition to its own running capacity.

domains.name: Governance & quality
domains.summary: Control access, discover assets, trace lineage, monitor quality, and govern AI interactions.
domains.billingContext: Built-in governance is distinct from billable monitoring, maintenance, storage, and AI usage.

domains.name: Sharing & collaboration
domains.summary: Exchange data products and collaborate with partners through governed sharing services.
domains.billingContext: Sharing can involve compute, storage, transfer, and provider charges; a missing catalog rate does not mean free.

domains.name: Platform & infrastructure
domains.summary: Understand compute, notebooks, storage, networking, and development experiences beneath workloads.
domains.billingContext: Classic VM charges, retained data, and network traffic can sit outside a workload's Databricks usage.

journeys.name: Source to business dashboard
journeys.summary: One possible analytics pattern: ingest operational data, transform it, query it, and publish insights. Connect already uses pipelines internally; model your actual execution without counting it twice.

journeys.name: Documents to a retrieval app
journeys.summary: An illustrative custom-agent architecture: prepare documents, retrieve relevant context, serve the agent, and expose an app. Choose model, embedding, and evaluation services for your own requirements.

journeys.name: Trusted data to a marketplace
journeys.summary: A provider can govern assets with Unity Catalog, share them with OpenSharing, and distribute them through Marketplace. These are collaboration roles, not a sequence of mandatory additional charges.

journeys.name: Postgres to an operational app
journeys.summary: Use Lakebase for transactional state and Databricks Apps for the user interface. Genie One can provide a business-user entry point; external apps and other entry points are also possible.
